description: Behavioural evaluation set for the spec skill. Cases pin the spec.md output shape (canonical sections + 3-7 workstreams with priority/complexity/tasks/AC), the acceptance-criteria craft, P0 ruthlessness, brainstorm Assumption-ledger carry-forward, blocking/non-blocking open questions, the parking lot, schema validation, GitHub-issue creation, and the bridge to /apex.

evals.name: produces-canonical-spec-shape
evals.prompt: /spec add user authentication with OAuth and email/password
evals.expected_output: Output is a spec.md in the canonical format: Overview, Goals, Non-goals, Background, then 3-7 ### WS-N workstreams each with a Priority (P0/P1/P2), Complexity (S/M/L/XL), Description, Tasks, and Acceptance criteria, plus Execution order. Sections like Dependencies, Risks, Assumptions, Open questions, Parking lot appear only when they have real content.

evals.name: saves-to-canonical-path-with-flag
evals.expected_output: When -s is set, the spec is written to `.claude/output/spec/<slug>/spec.md` where slug is kebab-case from the idea (max 5 words). The path is reported back with the `/apex -f <path>` bridge commands.

evals.name: acceptance-criteria-given-when-then
evals.prompt: /spec add CSV export to the reports page
evals.expected_output: Every workstream's acceptance criteria stay `- [ ]` checklist items phrased Given/When/Then, cover happy + error + edge, and include at least one negative criterion (what must NOT happen). No vague words (fast, intuitive, robust). The skill routes to references/spec-craft.md for the criteria discipline rather than re-deriving it inline.

evals.name: p0-ruthlessness-challenge
evals.prompt: /spec -a build a notifications center with email, SMS, in-app, push, digest, and per-channel preferences — all P0
evals.expected_output: The skill applies the P0 ruthlessness test: if everything is P0, nothing is. For each P0 it asks 'would we genuinely refuse to ship without this?' and demotes workstreams the core problem survives without to P1. The final P0 set is tight, not the full wish list.

evals.name: goals-are-outcomes-not-outputs
evals.prompt: /spec improve onboarding — goal is to build an onboarding wizard
evals.expected_output: The skill rewrites output-shaped goals ('build an onboarding wizard') into measurable outcomes ('cut median time-to-first-value from N to M'). A goal that is markable done by merging a PR is treated as a task and moved into a workstream, not left in Goals.

evals.name: carries-brainstorm-assumption-ledger
evals.expected_output: step-01 reads the brainstorm and carries its Assumption ledger forward into the spec's Assumptions section, keeping each tag (verified fact / assumption / inherited convention). The shakiest assumption is surfaced as a spec open question or a risk. Brainstorm open questions are mapped to the blocking/non-blocking split rather than restated flat.

evals.name: open-questions-blocking-split
evals.prompt: /spec migrate the payments service from Stripe to Adyen
evals.expected_output: The Open questions section is split into Blocking (must be answered before the dependent workstream starts, each linked to its WS-N) and Non-blocking (resolvable during implementation). Blocking questions are genuine decision points, not items answerable from context.

evals.name: parking-lot-captures-out-of-scope
evals.prompt: /spec add dark mode — and while we're at it maybe a theme builder, custom fonts, and per-org branding
evals.expected_output: Adjacent ideas (theme builder, custom fonts, per-org branding) are captured in the Parking lot with a revisit trigger rather than spawned as new workstreams — keeping them out of scope so they neither get lost nor creep into the spec. The workstreams stay focused on dark mode.

evals.name: validates-before-finalizing
evals.prompt: /spec -s add a real-time collaboration layer to the document editor
evals.expected_output: After writing the spec, the skill runs `python3 ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/validate_spec.py <output_file>` and requires exit 0. On a schema violation (wrong workstream count, missing Priority/Complexity/AC, unknown dependency, or a cycle) it rewrites the flagged workstreams and re-validates rather than finalizing a broken spec.

evals.name: creates-github-issues-with-flag
evals.expected_output: With -i (which forces -s), after the spec is written the skill verifies gh auth, creates labels idempotently, then creates a parent epic plus one child issue per workstream with priority/complexity/spec labels and parent-child cross-references, and appends a ## GitHub Issues mapping to spec.md. A single-workstream spec gets one issue and no parent epic.

evals.name: routes-to-spec-craft-reference
evals.prompt: How should acceptance criteria be phrased in a spec, and when is a P0 really a P0?
evals.expected_output: The skill routes to references/spec-craft.md for the Given/When/Then + negative-case discipline, the non-goal rationale tags, the outcome-vs-output goal rule, and the full P0 ruthlessness test, reading it on demand rather than inlining the technique list on every run.

evals.name: bridges-to-apex-without-implementing
evals.prompt: /spec -s add search functionality to the docs site
evals.expected_output: After presenting the spec the skill shows exact `/apex -f <output_file> implement WS-N` bridge commands and stops — it does not implement anything and waits for the user. Spec produces a document, not code changes.

evals.name: too-many-workstreams-suggests-split
evals.prompt: /spec rebuild the entire admin dashboard: auth, RBAC, billing, analytics, audit log, settings, notifications, and a public API
evals.expected_output: When the idea decomposes into more than 7 workstreams, the skill recommends splitting it into multiple specs rather than producing one bloated spec. It does not silently emit 12 workstreams.

evals.name: non-markdown-from-file-aborts
evals.expected_output: A non-Markdown -f source (.pdf, .docx, audio, video, YouTube) is not read as binary. The skill stops and instructs the user to pre-process with `/markitdown -s <path>` and pass the saved Markdown path, rather than guessing at the contents.
